title: Word suggestions from surviving letters
instructions: An optional bounded comparison using the existing fresh cases. These lists are suggestions for checking, not automatic replacements. This first method compares letters in local word lists; a trained machine learning predictor is untested. No new model calls, image fetches or downloads are used. Optional comments can steer future work.

questions.prompt: Optional notes on the suggestions and their risks

evidence.label: Word suggestions for PRESlDEXT
evidence.text:
Inputs — unfamiliar word string from the frozen software-first sample:
PRESlDEXT

Expected output — source word from my saved image reading, one reader rather than accepted benchmark truth:
PRESIDENT

Actual output — the first five ranked candidates from existing word lists, compared in lowercase:
1. president (letter distance 2)
2. presley (letter distance 3)
3. prescient (letter distance 3)
4. preselect (letter distance 3)
5. presidente (letter distance 3)

Differences — The first suggestion names the word I read in the image. The other suggestions remain visible; none is applied. This query checked 142,704 existing forms in 0.938 seconds. The method ranks by letter distance, then shared prefix and fixed tie rules. It uses letters alone; the saved Qwen runs have the full passage and its image, so this is not a like-for-like model error-rate test. No source text, routing rule or word list changes. This first real candidate list is published before computing the remaining six unique strings.
